proposals.before: Taizu became emperor of the north; Taizong ruled China. Purple-silver sable, baskets of gauze and silk—herds of loads arrived.
proposals.after: Taizu became emperor of the north; Taizong ruled China. Purple-silver sable, baskets of gauze and silk—loads arrived in abundance.
proposals.reason: Chinese 麇載 means abundant piled loads, not literal herds; 'herds of loads' is a mistranslation that obscures the sense.

proposals.before: Thereafter Tang took the regalia crown and blue-green robes as sacrificial dress, tongtian hats and crimson robes as court dress, and plain headcloths with robe-trousers as everyday dress.
proposals.after: Thereafter, Tang took the regalia crown and blue-green robes as sacrificial dress, tongtian hats and crimson robes as court dress, and plain headcloths with robe-trousers as everyday dress.
proposals.reason: Chinese 厥後唐 means 'thereafter, Tang'; the comma prevents misreading the false compound 後唐 (Later Tang).

decisions.reason: In 麇載而至, 麇 marks dense abundance of loads, not animal herds; 'herds of loads' misreads the figure, and 'loads arrived in abundance' restores the sense.
厥後唐 is already correctly rendered as 'Thereafter Tang'; English 'Thereafter' cannot be read as the dynasty name Later Tang (後唐), so the added comma is merely stylistic.
